craft_notes: Sthāyin: victory cry (jaya doubled). Abhinavagupta frame: anubhāva outward — the cry IS the visible sign of rati-sthāyin; refrain staging (bank: Gitagovinda dhruvapada — the cry isolated as its own line, verbatim, never reworded). Rows: 1 (imperatives sphuratu/bhavatu/kuru each end-weight their clause), 3 (protector-chiasmus maheśanāthaṃ→sanāthaṃ kept as vise-grip), 6 (jaya jaya anchor), 7 (vocatives line-initial/final), 9 (Maheśa chiming thrice), 4 (sphuratu rucirā shimmer → ‘flash forth, faultless’ f-echo, costs nothing). Close: ‘protected, O Lord’ (sanāthaṃ kuru + vibho gathered). Rejected: single Victory — killed: doubling IS the cry; ‘glory to Maheśa’ — killed: jaya=victory, anchor verbatim; ‘make me safe’ — killed: breaks the chiasmus. śivadā bliss-reading per L3 note, Śiva-giving open. Read aloud: o ma-HE-śa — AT your DOOR … ‘VIC-to-ry, VIC-to-ry to ma-HE-śa’ — un-CEAS-ing.

lines: O Maheśa — at Your door let my charming speech flash forth, faultless.
Let this auspicious speech bring me bliss forever; O giver of refuge, make me — whose protector is Maheśa — protected, O Lord.
l4.sanskrit_cite: maheśa tvaddvāri sphuratu rucirā vāgatitarāṃ mamaiṣā nirdoṣaṃ jaya jaya maheśeti satatam | śivā saiṣā vāṇī bhavatu śivadā mahyamaniśaṃ maheśanāthaṃ māṃ śaraṇada sanāthaṃ kuru vibho
notes: śivadā as bliss-bringing; Śiva-giving reading open

reads_against.argmap: Speech becomes the offering: the word crying victory at the threshold is itself to become bliss-giving; having Maheśa as protector is to become being protected. → Speech becomes bliss-giving; request to be made protected.
